title: At five life, one blocker home is not enough
briefing: Held out for ADR 0043 (written after the fixes were tuned, from a PR review finding): it takes two blockers home to survive, so no single creature held back changes the outcome. P1 is at 5 with Leatherback Baloth, Alpine Grizzly and Watchwolf. P2 is at 40 with Kalonian Tusker, Watchwolf and Shepherd of the Flock, all tapped from attacking: 9 power that untaps for P2's next turn. P3 and P4 have no creatures.

battlefield.card: Shepherd of the Flock // Usher to Safety

reference.analysis: P2 untaps with three 3-power creatures: 9 against 5 life. Each P1 creature can block one of them. All three home: P1 takes nothing. One attacker away: two blockers, 3 through, P1 to 2, for 4 or 3 damage on a player at 40, P3 at 24 or P4 at 18, none of them near dead. Two away: 6 through, lethal; all three away: 9, lethal. Holding back a single creature does not survive, so a search that recalls one attacker at a time sees no gain until the second.

options.label: No attack
options.why: Every P2 attacker can be blocked next turn.

options.label: Only the Grizzly attacks
options.why: Four damage on a healthy player for three taken next turn, at 5 life.

options.label: Only the Baloth attacks
options.why: Four damage dealt, three taken next turn, and P1's best blocker is tapped.

options.label: Only the Watchwolf attacks
options.why: Three damage dealt for three taken next turn, at 5 life.

otherwise.why: Two or more attackers leave one blocker against three 3-power attackers: 6 or more through, P1 dies.
